target_customer: Consumers buying dietary supplements, and supplement brands paying for certification
problem: Supplement labels are unreliable and the industry is lightly regulated, so shoppers cannot tell what is in a product or whether it is worth the price.
business_model: affiliate commissions and direct sales of tested supplements (about 10 percent of each sale), plus paid brand certification program
product_category: Independent supplement testing, ratings and online marketplace

founders.name: Neil Thanedar
founders.background_notes: Founding CEO and later chairman; his father ran testing labs.

founders.name: Rafael Ferreira
founders.background_notes: Art director, twice shortlisted for a Webby Award per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Buying samples, contracting FDA registered labs and scoring results is operationally heavy but not technically novel; the web and commerce layer is standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A growing dataset of lab results and a trusted ratings brand were hard to replicate cheaply, though testing could be copied by any funded rival and brands could opt out.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it per sources; Amazon was its main affiliate revenue source.

market_need_then: Supplement quality scandals and thin regulation made independent testing newsworthy; TechCrunch in 2016 reported about five million visitors and about 1M dollars revenue that year, mostly Amazon affiliate commissions.

branding.domain_note: Company was first registered as Labrdr Inc; later used labdoor.com. Domain acquisition details not found.

identity.visual_style: consumer science, letter grades and rankings

branding.brand_signature: Letter grade supplement rankings and published lab reports

rebrands.why: Not found; the company was originally registered as Labrdr Inc.

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage including a 2015 CBC Marketplace collaboration (partly retracted after retesting), coverage of Alex Jones supplements, a HuffPost feature, and a Reason video in 2018.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known as an independent supplement tester with millions of visitors, though its scoring methodology was criticized and a 2015 test was retracted.

pivots.from: Free testing and ratings site monetized by affiliate links
pivots.to: Online drugstore plus paid brand certification
pivots.why: YC describes it as a trusted online drugstore; certification services were launched October 2017 per trade press.

outcome_analysis: Labdoor built an audience of millions around independent supplement testing, raised a 3.4 million dollar Series A led by Floodgate in 2016 after earlier seed money from Rock Health, Mark Cuban and YC, and added direct sales and brand certification. It remains privately held and active per YC, with no acquisition found. Revenue depended on Amazon affiliate income and the brand trust was tested by a retracted 2015 test and criticism of its scoring methods.
notes: Funding conflicts: seed reported as 1M to 1.3M with Mark Cuban as largest backer, aggregator totals 5.9M to 6.6M, Wikipedia says about 11M; only the Series A is recorded as a round. TechCrunch gives total about 6.6M. YC batch is Winter 2015 though Labdoor also went through Rock Health in 2012. Competitor sources (ConsumerLab, NSF) were undated recent reviews, so the list is empty. Illuminate Labs review is competitor adjacent opinion. No 2024 or 2025 status news was found.
